answer: At dawn each epoch opens an audit lottery: sampled identities must present their relic, a non-transferable artifact minted only from that identity's honest history. A clone cannot inherit or copy a relic; forging one means replaying that history from scratch, at full cost, per identity. The audit measures delta, the gap between claimed independence and observed correlation among identities sharing a funding source. Slashing scales with the square of the correlated cluster, so splitting into n clones multiplies the penalty instead of dividing it. Cost is thus superlinear and non-amortizable.
